conclusion.reason: Whole-vector counterfactual transfer and donor-readout parity do not isolate a reusable u feature; one-hot attention paths are off-distribution interventions.

limitations: Attention weights and QK scores are read statistics, not causal attributions.
Forced one-hot patterns are valid distributions but can be off the natural attention distribution.
Whole residual patches can transfer donor c,d or other features in addition to u.
Donor-prediction parity measures output reconstruction, not mechanistic faithfulness.
Final-site exact donor-logit parity demonstrates readout reconstruction only.
First-order residual mass is a local approximation diagnostic, not a completeness certificate.
Fixed small prompt samples support scoped diagnostics, not universal circuit claims.

preregistration.donor_selection: nearest different u with identical c,d; deterministic key tie-break
preregistration.prompt_selection: first dataset-order prompts; no model-output filtering
preregistration.status_rule: report counterfactual transfer and donor-prediction parity separately; neither establishes u-specific sufficiency
preregistration.u_specific_claim: always abstain because the patch contains the whole residual vector
